title: Household room is layered across resources, tenure, liquidity, and credit
source_unit: Cross-source synthesis of SIPP person-record/month comparisons and Federal Reserve SHED adult and consent-linked credit-record measures

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SIPP tenure and resource comparison

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; outcome-specific nonblank universes

observations.method: SIPP WPFINWGT with REPWGT1-REPWGT240; Fay BRR with perturbation factor 0.5; comparison preserves outcome-specific nonblank universes.
observations.uncertainty: Design-based standard errors are available in the underlying four-cell estimates; differences here are descriptive and are not a common-household or causal tenure estimate.
observations.subgroup: Owned/bought versus rented, within monthly income-to-poverty bands below 1.00x and at least 4.00x.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local prices, household composition, debt, health, housing quality, repair and insurance obligations, and selection into tenure may explain part or all of the differences.

denominator.unit: published adult percentage bases; linked balance comparison conditional on consenting credit-card holders

unable_to_pay_400.unit: percent of adults; no listed means

credit_card_balance_carrying.unit: percent of credit-card owners in prior 12 months

hardship_group_balance_change.unit: US dollars, 2023 to 2025, among linked respondents reporting difficulty getting by

comfortable_group_balance_change.unit: US dollars, 2023 to 2025, among linked respondents living comfortably

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED published emergency-liquidity and credit measures plus descriptive comparison of consent-linked nationwide credit records by reported financial well-being.
observations.uncertainty: Hypothetical capacity, self-reported use, and linked credit records have different universes; the linked sample is consent-based and the balance comparison does not identify cause, repayment, delinquency, or a representative population effect.
observations.subgroup: All adults, credit-card owners, and linked credit-card respondents classified by reported financial comfort.
observations.counterinterpretation: Non-cash emergency responses may reflect precautionary buffer management; balance growth may reflect spending, rates, income, refinancing, or other events rather than hardship causing debt.

related_sources.claim: SHED savings measures distinguish current liquidity management from longer-run retirement actions.
Aggregate household debt provides market context but not a common household-level exposure path.

boundary: Bounded cross-source synthesis. It does not create a common-person household-room index or establish a causal tenure, price, credit, or hardship effect; it does not measure dated events, time/care substitution, recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
